title: The bishop pair
line: Two bishops on an open board. Keep them, and open lines for them.

steps.text: Two bishops together reach squares of both colors. On an open board, with few pawns in the way, this bishop pair is strong.
Tap a black pawn on a dark square. Of your bishops, only the one on f4 can attack it. Your other bishop takes care of the light squares.
steps.hint: The bishop on f4 stands on a dark square. Find black pawns on squares of the same color.
steps.after: With both bishops, no pawn is out of reach. A single bishop only ever sees half the board.

steps.text: Here the pawns are locked, and the bishops' roads are shut by pawns. A knight jumps over pawns, so they do not stop it.
Black's knight attacks your bishop, to trade itself for it. Keep your pair: step the bishop back.

wrong.d2d4: Then the knight takes your bishop, and Black has the two bishops instead.

steps.hint: The bishop has one safe square back along its diagonal, next to your queen.
steps.after: The bishop is safe. Black takes space on the left.

steps.text: Now open the center for your bishops. Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares.
steps.after: Pawns start to come off, and lines open for the bishops.

summary: Two bishops cover both colors and grow strong on an open board. Keep them, and open the position for them.
